observations: Alphabet disclosed Cloud growth of 48%, a greater-than-$70B annual run rate and $240B backlog in its 2025 Q4 earnings call, with AI demand cited as a driver.
Alphabet guided 2026 capital expenditures to $175B-$185B to meet demand and pursue AI opportunities.
Alphabet agreed to acquire Intersect for $4.75B plus assumed debt to accelerate data-center and energy capacity, including multiple gigawatts of projects in development or construction.
risks: The scale of planned capex raises return-on-invested-capital and execution risk if AI monetization lags infrastructure deployment.
Energy and data-center development exposes Alphabet to permitting, grid interconnection, construction and power-market constraints.
unknowns: Current 2026 quarterly realization versus the initial $175B-$185B capex plan was not established by the retrieved primary sources.
Intersect transaction close status and post-close integration contribution require current verification.

observations: Cloud backlog and revenue growth provide operating evidence that AI infrastructure spending is paired with customer demand, while the Intersect transaction targets a known physical constraint: power and data-center capacity.
The principal execution test is whether very high infrastructure investment converts into durable Cloud/AI revenue and cash returns rather than merely capacity growth.
risks: Large capex commitments can compress free cash flow and magnify forecasting errors.
AI product competition and rapid model/hardware shifts can shorten the useful economic life of infrastructure assumptions.
unknowns: Scout does not infer valuation or numeric factor scores.
Updated 2026 operating results are required for current execution calibration.
